headline: The American Football Master 20
threshold: By Lesson 20, you can teach a technique and check it with a teach-back, explain a lineup or schedule change to players and parents, say no to an unsafe request, lead a lightning or injury emergency, and write the game-day report in Spanish.

lessons.title: Why Our Inside Zone Sets Up Play-Action
lessons.objective: Explain how the inside zone run sets up play-action and have a new quarterback explain it back.

words.note: Loanword commonly used by Spanish-speaking coaches and broadcasters.
Used for defenders who react to a fake: los linebackers muerden la finta.
Loanword; the QB rolls out away from the run fake.

words.en: First we run inside zone 3 or 4 times.
words.es: Primero corremos la zona interior 3 o 4 veces.

words.en: That's why the linebackers bite on the fake.
words.es: Por eso los linebackers muerden la finta.

words.en: Then we fake it and look for the space behind them.
words.es: Luego hacemos la finta y buscamos el espacio detrás.

words.en: They bite because the line blocks just like on the run.
words.es: Muerden porque la línea bloquea igual que en la carrera.

words.en: Look at this clip: watch the linebacker.
words.es: Fíjate en este clip: mira al linebacker.
words.note: Informal (tú). Personal a before a person: mira al linebacker.

words.en: Now you explain it to me, step by step.
words.es: Ahora explícamelo tú, paso por paso.
words.note: Informal (tú), coach to player.

words.en: Close, but why do the linebackers bite?
words.es: Casi, pero ¿por qué muerden los linebackers?

words.en: If we don't sell the fake, play-action doesn't work.
words.es: Si no vendemos la finta, el play-action no funciona.

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI is Mateo Fuentes, a transfer quarterback: explain how our inside zone sets up play-action, then have him teach it back to you, using primero, luego, porque and por eso.

grammar.focus: Connectors for sequence and cause (primero, luego, porque, por eso: primero corremos la zona, por eso los linebackers muerden la finta)

examples.es: Primero corremos la zona interior, por eso los linebackers dan un paso al frente.
examples.en: First we run inside zone, so the linebackers step up.

examples.es: Luego hacemos la finta porque el segundo nivel ya está pensando en la carrera.
examples.en: Then we fake the handoff because the second level is already thinking run.

lessons.title: Teaching Heads-Up Tackling to Ten-Year-Olds
lessons.objective: Teach the steps of a safe, head-up tackle to youth players and check that they understand them.

words.note: Spanish uses the singular: baja la cadera = lower your hips.
For a woman: la entrenadora; for a man: el entrenador.

words.en: Stop! Everyone, listen for a moment.
words.note: Plural ustedes command to the whole group.

words.en: You lower your hips and look at the opponent.
words.es: Se baja la cadera y se mira al rival.

words.en: If you drop your head, you can't see anything.
words.es: Si bajas la cabeza, no ves nada.
words.note: Informal (tú), coach to a child.

words.en: You make contact with the shoulder, never with the head.
words.es: Se hace contacto con el hombro, nunca con la cabeza.

words.en: Nico, show me how it's done, slowly.
words.es: Nico, enséñame cómo se hace, despacio.
words.note: Informal (tú).

words.en: Lucía, can you work with him while I keep going with the others?
words.es: Lucía, ¿puedes trabajar con él mientras sigo con los demás?
words.note: Informal (tú) between coworkers.

words.en: If anything hurts, tell me right away.
words.es: Si algo te duele, me avisas de inmediato.
words.note: Informal (tú).

words.en: Ma'am, here we teach tackling with the head up.
words.es: Señora, aquí se enseña a taclear con la cabeza arriba.
words.note: Formal, to a parent. Taclear is common US and Mexican usage.

lessons.speaking: You are the youth coach, and the AI is Nico Alvarado, a 10-year-old player: teach the steps of a safe heads-up tackle and have him explain them back, using impersonal se (se baja la cadera) and si + present (si miras al rival, ves hacia dónde va).

grammar.focus: Impersonal se; si + present for general truths (se baja la cadera, se mira al rival; si bajas la cabeza, no ves nada)

examples.es: Se dan pasos cortos antes del contacto.
examples.en: You take short steps before contact.

examples.es: Si miras al rival, ves hacia dónde va.
examples.en: If you look at the opponent, you see where he's going.

lessons.title: Training a New Long Snapper Before Saturday
lessons.objective: Coach a new long snapper through grip, snap and follow-through, then have him teach it back.

words.note: Loanword used by Spanish-speaking coaches and players.
In Mexico, agujetas means laces, on shoes and on the ball.

words.en: Grip it like this, with your fingers on the laces.
words.es: Agárralo así, con los dedos sobre las agujetas.
words.note: Informal (tú). Pronoun attaches to the end of a positive command.

words.en: Release it fast and follow through with your hands back.
words.es: Suéltalo rápido y sigue con las manos hacia atrás.

words.en: Don't look at it, look at me.
words.es: No lo mires, mírame a mí.
words.note: In a negative command the pronoun goes before the verb: no lo mires.

words.en: It's sailing on you; aim it lower.
words.es: Se te está subiendo; apúntalo más abajo.

words.en: Relax, ignore the rushers and make your snap.
words.es: Tranquilo, ignora a los que vienen y haz tu snap.

words.en: Do it 10 more times, no rush.
Now you teach it to me: how do you grip it?
Coach, is it okay with you if we repeat the drill tomorrow?
words.es: Entrenador, ¿le parece bien si repetimos el ejercicio mañana?
words.note: Formal (usted), to the head coach.

lessons.speaking: You are the special teams coach, and the AI is Diego Salazar, a walk-on learning to long snap: coach his grip, snap and follow-through, then have him teach it back, using commands with pronouns like agárralo así, suéltalo rápido and mírame a mí.

grammar.focus: Commands with object pronouns (agárralo así, suéltalo rápido, no lo mires, mírame a mí)

examples.es: Suéltalo con las dos manos al mismo tiempo.
examples.en: Release it with both hands at the same time.

examples.es: No lo levantes; mándalo directo a mis manos.
examples.en: Don't lift it; send it straight to my hands.

lessons.title: Read the Helmet Fit Guide With the Equipment Manager
lessons.objective: Read a helmet maker's fit guide and explain each fitting step to a freshman before his first padded practice.

words.note: For a woman: la encargada de equipo.

words.en: Before you put it on, we need to measure your head.
words.es: Antes de ponértelo, hay que medir tu cabeza.
words.note: Informal (tú), to the player.

words.en: According to the guide, the rim sits 1 inch above the eyebrows.
words.es: Según la guía, el borde queda 1 pulgada arriba de las cejas.

words.en: After you buckle it, move your head; the helmet shouldn't spin.
words.es: Después de abrocharlo, mueve la cabeza; el casco no debe girar.

words.en: Tell me if it's tight or if anything hurts.
words.es: Avísame si te aprieta o te duele algo.
words.note: Informal (tú).

words.en: Óscar, the recertification date has passed; look at the label.
words.es: Óscar, la fecha de recertificación ya pasó; mira la etiqueta.
words.note: Informal (tú) between coworkers.

words.en: We set it aside and don't give it to anyone.
words.es: Lo apartamos y no se lo damos a nadie.

words.en: We need to ask the head coach before issuing another one.
words.es: Hay que preguntarle al entrenador principal antes de entregar otro.

words.en: Coach, do you want us to order a new one from the supplier?
words.es: Entrenador, ¿usted quiere que pidamos uno nuevo al proveedor?
words.note: Formal (usted), to the head coach.

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI is Tomás Rivera, a freshman before his first padded practice: read the helmet maker's fit guide with him and explain each fitting step in order, using antes de / después de + infinitive and hay que.

grammar.focus: Antes de / después de + infinitive; hay que (antes de abrochar el barbiquejo, hay que revisar las almohadillas según el fabricante)

examples.es: Antes de inflar las almohadillas, hay que leer la guía del fabricante.
examples.en: Before inflating the pads, you have to read the manufacturer's guide.

examples.es: Después de ponerte el protector bucal, hay que abrochar el barbiquejo.
examples.en: After putting in your mouthguard, you have to buckle the chin strap.

lessons.title: Torn Turf Seam Found Before the Morning Walkthrough
lessons.objective: Describe a field problem found at dawn and propose a new practice plan to the athletic director.

words.note: Patricia is a woman; for a man say el director deportivo.
Common loanword among US coaches for a slow, no-contact run-through.
Hule means rubber in Mexico; this is the crumb rubber infill.

words.en: When I got here, the seam was already torn.
words.es: Cuando llegué, la costura ya estaba rota.

words.en: Ernesto saw it while he was checking the field at dawn.
words.es: Ernesto la vio mientras revisaba el campo al amanecer.

words.en: It was open about 2 feet, near the 30-yard line.
words.es: Estaba abierta como 2 pies, cerca de la línea de 30.

words.en: Good morning, Mrs. Ruiz; we found a problem on the field.
words.es: Señora Ruiz, buenos días; encontramos un problema en el campo.
words.note: Formal: you're talking to the athletic director.

words.en: We could do the walkthrough in the gym at 7.
words.es: Podríamos hacer el walkthrough en el gimnasio a las 7.

words.en: Ernesto, put caution tape around it, please.
words.es: Ernesto, pon cinta de precaución alrededor, por favor.
words.note: Informal tú between coworkers.

words.en: Let's not glue it ourselves; the technician should check it.
words.es: No la peguemos nosotros; mejor que la revise el técnico.

words.en: Would it be OK with you if we call the warranty company today?
words.es: ¿Le parecería bien si llamamos hoy a la empresa de la garantía?
words.note: Formal.

lessons.speaking: You are the head coach, and the AI is athletic director Patricia Ruiz: on the phone, describe the torn turf seam you found using the preterite and imperfect (cuando llegué, estaba rota), and propose a new walkthrough plan with podríamos and sería mejor.

grammar.focus: Preterite vs imperfect; conditional for the proposal (cuando llegué, la costura estaba rota; podríamos usar el gimnasio)

examples.es: Cuando llegué, Ernesto revisaba la costura cerca de la línea de 30 yardas.
examples.en: When I arrived, Ernesto was checking the seam near the 30-yard line.

examples.es: Sería más seguro mover a los jugadores al gimnasio.
examples.en: It would be safer to move the players to the gym.

lessons.title: Two Linemen Ineligible: Moving a Tight End to Tackle
lessons.objective: Explain a lineup substitution to the line coach and compare the options for Friday's game.

words.note: Used in US schools; you can also say no es elegible.

words.en: Andrés is faster than Bruno, but lighter.
words.es: Andrés es más rápido que Bruno, pero menos pesado.

words.en: Bruno weighs 25 pounds more than Andrés.
words.es: Bruno pesa 25 libras más que Andrés.

words.en: Andrés is going to play right tackle on Friday.
words.es: Andrés va a jugar de tackle derecho el viernes.

words.en: Bruno hasn't started a single game yet.
words.es: Bruno todavía no ha jugado ningún partido como titular.

words.en: Coach Delgado, which option seems safer to you?
words.es: Coach Delgado, ¿qué opción le parece más segura?
words.note: Formal usted with a fellow coach; players and coaches often say Coach.

words.en: This week we're going to work on footwork with Andrés.
words.es: Esta semana vamos a trabajar el juego de pies con Andrés.

words.en: If we move Andrés, we'll lose our best tight end.
words.es: Si movemos a Andrés, perderemos a nuestro mejor tight end.

words.en: Bruno, listen, you're going into the rotation; get ready.
words.es: Bruno, oye, vas a entrar en la rotación; prepárate.
words.note: Informal tú with a player.

lessons.speaking: You are the offensive coordinator, and the AI is line coach Henry Delgado: explain who is ineligible, compare Andrés and Bruno with más… que and menos… que, and lay out Friday's plan with va a jugar and the future (jugará, practicaremos).

grammar.focus: Future and ir a; comparisons (Andrés es más rápido que Bruno pero menos pesado; va a jugar de tackle)

examples.es: Andrés es más ágil que Bruno, pero menos fuerte.
examples.en: Andrés is more agile than Bruno, but less strong.

examples.es: El viernes Andrés va a jugar de tackle y Bruno entrará en la rotación.
examples.en: On Friday Andrés is going to play tackle and Bruno will come in on the rotation.

lessons.title: College Scout at Practice Asks for the Numbers
lessons.objective: Answer a college scout's questions about a cornerback's season with exact stats and short game stories.

words.note: Brenda is a woman; for a man say el reclutador.
Decimals use a point in US and Mexican Spanish: 3.4, said tres punto cuatro.
The run after an interception or a kick.

words.en: He ran 40 yards in 4.6 seconds, according to the camp stopwatch.
words.es: Corrió 40 yardas en 4.6 segundos, según el cronómetro del campamento.

words.en: Against Lincoln, he returned an interception 60 yards for a touchdown.
words.es: Contra Lincoln, regresó una intercepción 60 yardas para touchdown.

words.en: He broke up 11 passes in 10 games, according to our stats.
words.es: Defendió 11 pases en 10 partidos, según nuestras estadísticas.

words.en: Excuse me, give me a second; I have to finish this drill.
words.es: Disculpe, deme un segundo; tengo que terminar este ejercicio.
words.note: Formal: you're talking to a visiting recruiter.

words.en: His GPA is 3.4, according to the counselor.
words.es: Su promedio es de 3.4, según la consejera.

words.en: I don't have that exact number; I'll confirm it for you today.
words.es: Ese dato no lo tengo exacto; se lo confirmo hoy.

words.en: Do you want me to send you his highlight video?
words.es: ¿Quiere que le mande el video de sus jugadas destacadas?
words.note: Formal.

lessons.speaking: You are Isaiah's defensive backs coach, and the AI is state university recruiter Brenda Whitfield: answer her questions about Isaiah's season with exact numbers and short game stories in the preterite (interceptó, corrió, defendió), and say where each stat comes from.

grammar.focus: Preterite narration; numbers under pressure (interceptó tres pases, corrió 40 yardas en 4.6 segundos según el cronómetro del campamento)

examples.es: En el partido contra Lincoln, Isaiah defendió 4 pases y forzó un fumble.
examples.en: In the game against Lincoln, Isaiah broke up 4 passes and forced a fumble.

examples.es: En el campamento saltó 36 pulgadas, según la hoja de medición.
examples.en: At camp he jumped 36 inches, according to the measurement sheet.

lessons.title: Saying No: Booster Wants Full Pads in the Midday Heat
lessons.objective: Refuse a booster's request for a full-pads midday practice and explain the safer plan instead.

words.note: For a woman, say la entrenadora atlética.
Pads is the usual loanword among US players and coaches.

words.en: Don Víctor, I don't recommend they practice at noon.
words.es: Don Víctor, no recomiendo que practiquen a mediodía.
words.note: Formal; Don + first name shows respect in Mexican Spanish.

words.en: The reading is 92 degrees Fahrenheit, according to the athletic trainer.
words.es: La lectura es de 92 grados Fahrenheit, según el entrenador atlético.

words.en: Under the school's heat policy, there are no pads today.
words.es: Según la política de calor de la escuela, hoy no hay pads.

words.en: Don't ask me that; I won't put the kids at risk.
words.es: No me pida eso; no voy a arriesgar a los muchachos.
words.note: Formal negative command (usted).

words.en: I understand the loss hurts, but the answer is no.
words.es: Entiendo que le duele la derrota, pero la respuesta es no.

words.en: Tomorrow we practice early, in helmets and shorts, with water breaks.
words.es: Mañana practicamos temprano, en casco y shorts, con descansos para agua.

words.en: Don't put pads on them today; just helmets and shorts.
words.es: No les pongan los pads hoy; solo casco y shorts.
words.note: Plural ustedes command to your assistant coaches.

words.en: If you'd like, I invite you to watch tomorrow's practice.
words.es: Si quiere, lo invito a ver la práctica de mañana.
words.note: Formal.

lessons.speaking: You are the head coach, and the AI is booster president Víctor Cordero: politely refuse his full-pads noon practice using negative commands and no recomiendo que + subjunctive, cite the athletic trainer's reading and the school's heat policy, and offer the safer plan.

grammar.focus: Negative commands; subjunctive after no recomiendo que (no les pongas los pads; no recomiendo que practiquen a mediodía)

examples.es: Raúl, no les pongas los pads; hoy solo practican en casco.
examples.en: Raúl, don't put pads on them; today they only practice in helmets.

examples.es: No recomiendo que practiquen a mediodía con este índice de calor.
examples.en: I don't recommend they practice at noon with this heat index.

lessons.title: Feedback for a Linebacker Who Freelances
lessons.objective: Give a linebacker specific, respectful feedback on leaving his gap and agree on what he will change.

words.note: Área is feminine but takes el in the singular: el área, las áreas.
Used with ponerse: no te pongas a la defensiva.

words.en: You lead us in tackles; nobody can take that from you.
words.es: Eres nuestro líder en tacleadas; eso nadie te lo quita.
words.note: Informal (tú). Start with real praise before the correction.

words.en: Watch this clip with me: where is your gap?
words.es: Mira este clip conmigo: ¿dónde está tu hueco?

words.en: Here you leave your gap and they run 40 yards.
words.es: Aquí sales de tu hueco y corren 40 yardas.

words.en: I'm not telling you this to scold you, but so you improve.
words.es: No te lo digo para regañarte, sino para que mejores.
words.note: Para que always takes the subjunctive.

words.en: I want you to close your gap before going after the ball.
words.es: Quiero que cierres tu hueco antes de buscar la pelota.

words.en: I recommend you trust the safety; he has that lane.
words.es: Te recomiendo que confíes en el safety; él tiene ese carril.

words.en: What do you think happens when you leave your gap?
words.es: ¿Qué crees que pasa cuando dejas tu hueco?

words.en: So, what do you commit to changing this week?
words.es: Entonces, ¿qué te comprometes a cambiar esta semana?

lessons.speaking: You are the defensive coach, and the AI is linebacker Julián Herrera: praise his tackling, show the clips where he leaves his gap, and agree on one change, using quiero que and te recomiendo que with the subjunctive.

grammar.focus: Present subjunctive after wishes and recommendations (quiero que te quedes en tu hueco; te recomiendo que confíes en el sistema)

examples.es: Quiero que te quedes en tu hueco aunque veas la pelota.
examples.en: I want you to stay in your gap even if you see the ball.

examples.es: Te recomiendo que veas estos clips otra vez esta noche.
examples.en: I recommend you watch these clips again tonight.

lessons.title: Settling a Locker Room Fight Over a Blown Route
lessons.objective: Hear both sides of a quarterback–receiver argument, report what each said, and agree on a fix.

words.note: Agrees with the person: Kevin está enojado; los dos están enojados.
Plural ustedes command, said to both players.

words.en: Mateo, you first; Kevin, your turn is after.
words.es: Mateo, tú primero; Kevin, te toca después.

words.en: Mateo said you broke before 12 yards.
words.es: Mateo dijo que tú cortaste antes de las 12 yardas.

words.en: Kevin said the safety was waiting for him inside.
words.es: Kevin dijo que el safety lo estaba esperando adentro.

words.en: So you were both reading a different coverage.
words.es: O sea, los dos leían una cobertura diferente.

words.en: Here nobody shoves a teammate, no matter what.
words.es: Aquí nadie empuja a un compañero, pase lo que pase.

words.en: Tomorrow the three of us watch the film with the coordinator.
words.es: Mañana los tres vemos el video con el coordinador.

words.en: Shake hands and let's move on as a team.
words.es: Dense la mano y sigamos como equipo.
words.note: Dense is the ustedes command of darse.

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI plays Mateo Fuentes and Kevin Ramírez: separate them, have each tell his version, report what each said with dijo que and the imperfect (la ruta era, el safety estaba), and agree on a fix.

grammar.focus: Reported speech; imperfect for background (Kevin dijo que la ruta era de diez yardas; Mateo dijo que el safety estaba encima)

examples.es: Kevin dijo que la ruta era de 10 yardas.
examples.en: Kevin said the route was 10 yards.

examples.es: Mateo explicó que el safety estaba encima cuando soltó el balón.
examples.en: Mateo explained that the safety was right on top when he released the ball.

lessons.title: Keeping the Toros Together After an 0-4 Start
lessons.objective: Rally a discouraged team after a fourth straight loss and commit to concrete goals for next week.

words.note: Common in Mexican football for penalties; you also hear las faltas.

words.en: Rodrigo, thanks for telling me; I'm going to talk to everyone.
words.es: Rodrigo, gracias por avisarme; voy a hablar con todos.
words.note: Informal (tú), to the captain.

words.en: Guys, turn off the music and listen to me, please.
words.es: Muchachos, apaguen la música y escúchenme, por favor.
words.note: Plural ustedes commands to the whole bus.

words.en: I know losing 4 in a row hurts; it hurts me too.
words.es: Sé que duele perder 4 seguidos; a mí también me duele.

words.en: Tomorrow at 10 we'll all watch the film together.
words.es: Mañana a las 10 veremos el video todos juntos.

words.en: On Saturday we'll commit fewer than 5 penalties; that's the goal.
words.es: El sábado cometeremos menos de 5 castigos; esa es la meta.

words.en: On Saturday we won't lose a single ball.
words.es: El sábado no perderemos ni un balón.

words.en: Nobody quits here; we started together and we finish together.
words.es: Aquí nadie se rinde; empezamos juntos y terminamos juntos.

words.en: Let's go, Toros! There's still a lot of season left!

lessons.speaking: You are the head coach, and the AI is captain Rodrigo Peña, then the whole bus: thank Rodrigo, then rally the team after the loss and commit to concrete goals for next week, using the future (veremos, ganaremos) and lines like ¡vamos, equipo!

grammar.focus: Future for commitments; encouragement register (mañana veremos el video, ganaremos la batalla en la línea, ¡vamos, equipo!)

examples.es: Mañana veremos el video y corregiremos los errores.
examples.en: Tomorrow we'll watch the film and fix the mistakes.

examples.es: Esta semana trabajaremos los fundamentos más que nunca.
examples.en: This week we'll work on the fundamentals more than ever.

lessons.title: Benched for Grades: Same News to Four Listeners
lessons.objective: Tell a benched player, his mother, the athletic director and a reporter the same news in the right register.

words.note: Estar en la banca = to sit on the bench.
Mexican usage; also la boleta de calificaciones.

words.en: Samuel, I have to tell you something, and it isn't easy.
words.es: Samuel, te tengo que decir algo, y no es fácil.
words.note: Informal (tú), coach to player.

words.en: This Friday you won't play, but you're still part of the team.
words.es: Este viernes no vas a jugar, pero sigues siendo del equipo.
words.note: Informal (tú).

words.en: Mrs. Ortiz, I'd like to explain why Samuel isn't playing Friday.
words.es: Señora Ortiz, quisiera explicarle por qué Samuel no juega el viernes.
words.note: Formal (usted); quisiera softens the request.

words.en: Would you like to meet with me and the counselor this week?
words.es: ¿Le gustaría reunirse conmigo y con la consejera esta semana?
words.note: Formal (usted).

words.en: Ms. Ruiz, I wanted to let you know Samuel won't play Friday.
words.es: Señora Ruiz, quería avisarle que Samuel no jugará el viernes.
words.note: Formal (usted); quería is softer than quiero.

words.en: He can come back as soon as he meets the district rules.
words.es: Podrá volver en cuanto cumpla con el reglamento del distrito.

words.en: Mr. Brooks, Samuel won't be available on Friday.
words.es: Señor Brooks, Samuel no estará disponible el viernes.
words.note: Formal (usted), to the reporter.

words.en: I'm sorry, for privacy reasons I can't give you academic details.
words.es: Lo siento, por privacidad no puedo darle detalles académicos.
words.note: Formal (usted).

lessons.speaking: You are the head coach, and the AI plays Samuel Ortiz, his mother, the athletic director and a reporter: give each the same benching news, switching between tú and usted, using softeners like quisiera explicarle and me gustaría, and keep his grades private.

grammar.focus: Usted / tú switching; softeners (Samuel, te tengo que decir algo; Señora Ortiz, quisiera explicarle; me gustaría hablar con usted)

examples.es: Samuel, te tengo que decir algo antes de la práctica.
examples.en: Samuel, I have to tell you something before practice.

examples.es: Señora Ortiz, quisiera explicarle la situación con calma.
examples.en: Mrs. Ortiz, I'd like to explain the situation to you calmly.

lessons.title: Heat Illness at Preseason Camp: Timeline for the EMTs
lessons.objective: Narrate a player's heat collapse minute by minute to EMTs and the trainer, then fill in the incident form.

words.note: Common US word for EMTs and paramedics alike.
Use confundida for a woman.
Say 'nueve once'.
Use la testigo for a woman.

words.en: At 9:40, Marcos started the conditioning sprints.
words.es: A las 9:40, Marcos empezó los sprints de acondicionamiento.

words.en: After the third sprint, he said he had cramps.
words.es: Después del tercer sprint, dijo que tenía calambres.

words.en: At 9:48 he collapsed near the 20-yard line.
words.es: A las 9:48 se cayó cerca de la línea de 20.

words.en: As soon as he collapsed, trainer Flores ran to him.
words.es: En cuanto se cayó, la entrenadora Flores corrió hacia él.

words.en: He was confused and didn't know where he was.
words.es: Estaba confundido y no sabía dónde estaba.

words.en: We called 911 at 9:50, two minutes later.
words.es: Llamamos al 911 a las 9:50, dos minutos después.

words.en: According to trainer Flores, his rectal temperature was 106 degrees Fahrenheit.
words.es: Según la entrenadora Flores, su temperatura rectal era de 106 grados Fahrenheit.
words.note: Always give the source of a medical reading; let the trainer confirm it.

words.en: Excuse me, she can give you the exact medical details.
words.es: Disculpen, ella les puede dar los datos médicos exactos.
words.note: Formal plural (ustedes) to the EMTs.

lessons.speaking: You are the assistant coach, and the AI is an arriving EMT, then the trainer: give a minute-by-minute timeline of Marcos's collapse in the past tense with time markers like a las 9:40, después del tercer sprint and en cuanto se cayó, then sum it up for the incident report.

grammar.focus: Past narration with time markers (a las 9:40, después del tercer sprint, en cuanto se cayó, diez minutos más tarde)

examples.es: Después del tercer sprint, Marcos se puso pálido y dejó de hablar.
examples.en: After the third sprint, Marcos turned pale and stopped talking.

examples.es: Diez minutos más tarde, llegó la ambulancia al campo.
examples.en: Ten minutes later, the ambulance reached the field.

lessons.title: Near Miss: The Blocking Sled Rolls on the Slope
lessons.objective: Talk through a near miss with the staff without blame and agree on what changes in the drill setup.

words.note: Standard US safety term; some say el incidente sin lesiones.
Use el voluntario for a man.

words.es: El trineo por poco golpea a Leo.
words.note: Personal a before Leo.

words.en: It could have been serious; luckily nobody got hurt.
words.es: Podría haber sido grave; por suerte nadie se lastimó.

words.en: We're not looking for someone to blame; we're looking for what to change.
words.es: Aquí no buscamos culpables; buscamos qué cambiar.

words.en: Felipe, what did you see from your side?
words.es: Felipe, ¿qué viste tú desde tu lado?
words.note: Informal (tú) between coaches.

words.en: Mrs. Quintero, will you help us find a flat spot?
words.es: Señora Quintero, ¿nos ayuda a buscar un lugar plano?
words.note: Formal (usted) to the volunteer.

words.en: If the line waits off to the side, nobody is in its path.
words.es: Si la fila espera a un lado, nadie queda en su camino.

words.en: Something serious almost happened, so we change it today.
words.es: Casi pasa algo serio, así que lo cambiamos hoy mismo.

lessons.speaking: You are the head coach, and the AI is assistant coach Felipe Arce: talk through the sled near miss without blaming anyone, using por poco golpea a Leo, podría haber sido grave and si clauses like si lo ponemos en plano, no se mueve, and agree on a new drill setup.

grammar.focus: Casi, por poco, podría haber; si clauses (el trineo por poco golpea a Leo; podría haber sido grave; si lo ponemos en plano, no se mueve)

examples.es: El trineo casi se le va encima a Leo.
examples.en: The sled almost ran right into Leo.

examples.es: Si lo ponemos en terreno plano, no se mueve.
examples.en: If we put it on flat ground, it doesn't move.

lessons.title: Lightning on Friday Night: Clearing Field and Stands
lessons.objective: Call a lightning stop over the radio, clear players and fans, and explain the restart rule.

words.note: In Mexico the device is el radio (masculine).

words.en: Mr. Grant, I saw lightning to the north; we have to stop now.
words.es: Señor Grant, vi un rayo al norte; hay que parar ya.
words.note: Formal (usted) to the referee.

words.en: Everyone to the locker room, now!
Gabriel, announce that everyone should go to their cars, please.
words.es: Gabriel, anuncia que todos vayan a sus carros, por favor.
words.note: Informal (tú) to a coworker.

words.en: Please don't stay in the stands; it isn't safe.
words.es: Por favor, no se queden en las gradas; no es seguro.
words.note: Ustedes to the fans.

words.en: According to the state policy, we wait 30 minutes after the last strike.
words.es: Según la política estatal, esperamos 30 minutos después del último rayo.

words.en: If we hear more thunder, the wait will start over.
words.es: Si escuchamos otro trueno, la espera empezará de cero.

words.en: Gabriel, over: has the whole crowd left yet?
words.es: Gabriel, cambio: ¿ya salió todo el público?
words.note: Cambio = over, at the end of a radio message.

words.en: If 30 minutes pass with no more lightning or thunder, the referee will decide when we resume.
words.es: Si pasan 30 minutos sin más rayos ni truenos, el árbitro decidirá cuándo reanudamos.

lessons.speaking: You are the head coach, and the AI is referee Thomas Grant, then announcer Gabriel Soto, on the radio: call the lightning stop, clear the field and stands with short commands like todos al vestuario, ya, and explain the restart rule with si + present → future.

grammar.focus: Si + present → future; short radio or phone commands (si vemos otro rayo, reiniciaremos la espera; todos al vestuario, ya)

examples.es: Si vemos otro rayo, reiniciaremos la espera.
examples.en: If we see another strike, we'll restart the wait.

examples.es: Jugadores, al vestuario, ya; no se detengan.
examples.en: Players, to the locker room, now; don't stop.

lessons.title: State Auditor Reviews Our Safety Records
lessons.objective: Walk a state association auditor through coach certifications, the emergency plan and concussion records.

words.note: Use el auditor for a man.
RCP = CPR; say 'erre ce pe'.

words.en: Welcome, Ms. Navarro; here is the emergency action plan.
words.es: Bienvenida, señora Navarro; aquí tiene el plan de emergencia.
words.note: Formal (usted).

words.en: The drill is practiced with all staff; here is the log.
words.es: Se practica el simulacro con todo el personal; aquí está la bitácora.

words.en: CPR certifications are renewed according to the state association.
words.es: Las certificaciones de RCP se renuevan según la asociación estatal.

words.en: Medical files are kept under lock and key in this cabinet.
words.es: Los expedientes médicos se guardan bajo llave en este archivero.

words.en: I'll gladly show you the dates, but the results are confidential.
words.es: Con gusto le muestro las fechas, pero los resultados son confidenciales.

words.en: Would you like me to make you a copy of the certifications?
words.es: ¿Desea que le saque una copia de las certificaciones?
words.note: Formal; saque is subjunctive after desea que.

words.en: I don't have that document here; I'll send it to you today.
words.es: Ese documento no lo tengo aquí; se lo envío hoy.

lessons.speaking: You are the athletic coordinator, and the AI is state auditor Elena Navarro: walk her through coach certifications, the emergency plan and concussion records in formal usted, using passive se (se revisan, se guardan) and keeping players' medical details private.

grammar.focus: Formal register; passive se for procedures (se revisan los cascos según el fabricante; se guardan los registros médicos bajo llave)

examples.es: Se revisa el desfibrilador según las indicaciones del fabricante.
examples.en: The AED is checked according to the manufacturer's instructions.

examples.es: Se guardan los registros médicos bajo llave, separados de los demás.
examples.en: Medical records are kept under lock and key, separate from the rest.

lessons.title: Writing the Post-Game Report for the League Office
lessons.objective: Write a clear post-game report covering the score, an ejection, an injury and the follow-up plan.

words.note: Alberto Gil is el comisionado; a woman would be la comisionada.
Written connector; always follow it with a comma.
Introduces a consequence, such as the follow-up plan.

words.en: Dear Commissioner Gil: I am sending you today's game report.
words.es: Estimado comisionado Gil: le envío el informe del partido de hoy.
words.note: Formal written opening; use a colon after the name, not a comma.

words.en: First, we won the game 28 to 21.
words.es: En primer lugar, ganamos el partido 28 a 21.

words.en: In addition, the referee ejected our number 54 for a late hit.
words.es: Además, el árbitro expulsó a nuestro número 54 por un golpe tardío.
words.note: Personal a: expulsó a nuestro número 54.

words.en: However, the player accepted the decision and left without protesting.
words.es: Sin embargo, el jugador aceptó la decisión y salió sin protestar.

words.en: In the third quarter, number 22 was taken to the hospital.
words.es: En el tercer cuarto, trasladaron al número 22 al hospital.

words.en: Out of respect for his privacy, I am not including medical details.
words.es: Por respeto a su privacidad, no incluyo detalles médicos.

words.en: Therefore, on Monday we will review tackling technique with everyone.
words.es: Por lo tanto, el lunes repasaremos la técnica de tacleo con todos.

words.en: I am attaching the referee's report and the video of the play.
words.es: Le adjunto el informe del árbitro y el video de la jugada.
words.note: Formal: le adjunto (I attach for you).

lessons.speaking: You are the Toros head coach, and the AI is league commissioner Alberto Gil: dictate your post-game report covering the score, the ejection, the injured player and the follow-up plan, using en primer lugar, además, sin embargo and por lo tanto, with no private medical details.

grammar.focus: Written register; report connectors (en primer lugar, además, sin embargo, por lo tanto, en resumen)

examples.es: Además, el número 54 fue expulsado por un golpe tardío en el segundo cuarto.
examples.en: In addition, number 54 was ejected for a late hit in the second quarter.

examples.es: En resumen, ganamos el partido, pero quedan dos asuntos pendientes.
examples.en: In short, we won the game, but two matters are still pending.

lessons.title: Bus Breakdown: Texting Parents and Calling the Other Coach
lessons.objective: Text parents a clear schedule change and politely call the opposing coach to ask to move kickoff.

words.note: Mexican usage for a bus; el autobús is also common.
Mexican term for the shoulder of the road.
Mexican stress: chofer, on the last syllable.

words.en: Coach Mendoza, good afternoon; I'm calling to let you know about a problem.
words.es: Entrenador Mendoza, buenas tardes; le llamo para avisarle de un problema.
words.note: Formal: le llamo, avisarle.

words.en: Would it be possible to start the game at 7:30?
words.es: ¿Sería posible empezar el partido a las 7:30?
words.note: Polite conditional: sería posible.

words.en: I understand your position; I wouldn't ask you this if it weren't necessary.
words.es: Entiendo su posición; no le pediría esto si no fuera necesario.
words.note: Formal; conditional plus imperfect subjunctive.

words.en: Could we check it with the referees and the league?
words.es: ¿Podríamos consultarlo con los árbitros y la liga?

words.en: Hi everyone: the bus broke down, but we are all fine.
words.es: Hola a todos: el camión se descompuso, pero todos estamos bien.
words.note: Text to parents: start with the reassurance.

words.en: We'll arrive about an hour late; I'll let you know about any change.
words.es: Llegaremos aproximadamente una hora tarde; les aviso de cualquier cambio.

words.en: The kids are staying inside the bus, away from the traffic.
words.es: Los muchachos se quedan dentro del camión, lejos del tráfico.

words.en: I'll send you a message as soon as the tow truck arrives.
words.es: Le mando un mensaje en cuanto llegue la grúa.

lessons.speaking: You are the Valle Verde youth coach, and the AI is opposing coach Javier Mendoza: first read aloud your text to the parents' group, then call him to explain the bus breakdown and politely ask to move kickoff, using le llamo para avisarle and ¿podría…?

grammar.focus: Phone and text conventions; conditional politeness (le llamo para avisarle; ¿podría retrasar el inicio media hora?)

examples.es: Le llamo para avisarle que vamos a llegar tarde.
examples.en: I'm calling to let you know that we are going to be late.

examples.es: ¿Podría esperarnos media hora más, por favor?
examples.en: Could you wait for us half an hour longer, please?

lessons.title: End-of-Season Meeting With a Senior and His Father
lessons.objective: Review a senior's season with him and his father and lay out the conditions for playing in college.

words.note: US Spanish for community college; also called colegio comunitario in official documents.

words.en: Mr. Morales, thank you for coming; Isaiah had a great season.
words.es: Señor Morales, gracias por venir; Isaiah tuvo una gran temporada.
words.note: Formal, to the father.

words.en: Isaiah, you could play in college as long as you keep improving.
words.es: Isaiah, podrías jugar en la universidad siempre que sigas mejorando.
words.note: Informal tú to the player; siempre que + subjunctive.

words.en: I can't promise you anything, but I can tell you what's still missing.
words.es: No le puedo prometer nada, pero sí le puedo decir qué falta.
words.note: Formal.

words.en: If I were you, I would ask for the offer in writing.
words.es: Si yo fuera usted, pediría la oferta por escrito.
words.note: Formal; si + imperfect subjunctive, then conditional.

words.en: As long as there's nothing in writing, it's not a real offer.
words.es: Mientras no haya nada por escrito, no es una oferta real.

words.en: I would help you put together your profile if you sent me your videos.
words.es: Te ayudaría a armar tu perfil si me mandaras tus videos.
words.note: Informal; conditional with si + imperfect subjunctive.

words.en: If the scholarship doesn't come through, community college is a good option.
words.es: Si no sale la beca, el colegio comunitario es buena opción.

words.en: What would you like to do, Isaiah, beyond football?
words.es: ¿Qué te gustaría hacer tú, Isaiah, más allá del fútbol americano?
words.note: Informal.

lessons.speaking: You are Isaiah's coach, and the AI is his father, Luis Morales: review Isaiah's season and explain what would need to happen for him to play in college without promising anything, using podrías… siempre que + subjunctive and conditionals like te ayudaría.

grammar.focus: Conditional; subjunctive in conditions (podrías jugar en la universidad siempre que mantengas tus notas; te ayudaría con los videos)

examples.es: Podrías recibir una beca siempre que termines el año con buenas notas.
examples.en: You could get a scholarship as long as you finish the year with good grades.

examples.es: Si entrenaras fuerza en la temporada baja, llamarías más la atención.
examples.en: If you did strength training in the offseason, you would draw more attention.

lessons.title: Capstone: Playoff Game Day From Sunrise to Report
lessons.objective: Lead a full playoff day in Spanish: teach, fix problems, handle an injury and weather, and file the report.

words.en: Mateo, go over it with me: if the safety comes up, throw it over the top.
words.es: Mateo, repásala conmigo: si el safety sube, lánzala por arriba.
words.note: Informal tú commands with attached pronouns.

words.en: Don't force it; if he's not open, throw it away.
words.es: No lo fuerces; si no está abierto, tíralo afuera.
words.note: Negative command: pronoun goes before the verb.

words.en: Diego has a fever, so Ramiro plays in his place today.
words.es: Diego tiene fiebre, así que hoy juega Ramiro en su lugar.

words.en: Nadia, what do you need me to do while you evaluate him?
words.es: Nadia, ¿qué necesitas que haga yo mientras lo evalúas?
words.note: Informal between coworkers; necesitas que + subjunctive.

words.en: He doesn't go back in until you clear him.
words.es: No vuelve a jugar hasta que tú lo autorices.
words.note: Hasta que + subjunctive for a future condition.

words.en: Guys, stay in the locker room until the referee gives the order.
words.es: Muchachos, quédense en el vestuario hasta que el árbitro dé la orden.
words.note: Ustedes command to the team; dé carries an accent.

words.en: Therefore, number 7 is out until further notice.
words.es: Por lo tanto, el número 7 queda fuera hasta nuevo aviso.

words.en: Mrs. Ruiz, I'll send you the report tonight, before 11.
words.es: Señora Ruiz, le envío el informe esta noche, antes de las 11.
words.note: Formal, to the athletic director.

lessons.speaking: You are Riverside High's head coach, and the AI is Mateo Fuentes, trainer Nadia Flores and others: re-teach Mateo a play with commands like lánzala, replace a sick starter, answer Nadia using hasta que + subjunctive, hold the weather delay and dictate the night's report with connectors.

grammar.focus: Capstone: integrating the Master 20 grammar (connectors, commands with pronouns, subjunctive, si clauses, formal and written register)

examples.es: Si el safety se queda arriba, dásela al corredor.
examples.en: If the safety stays deep, hand it to the running back.

examples.es: En primer lugar, ganamos 21 a 14; sin embargo, el número 7 salió lesionado.
examples.en: First, we won 21 to 14; however, number 7 left the game injured.
